content.text:
All three cases throw the right exception with a descriptive message. Here's the full picture:

**Exception hierarchy** (all unchecked — null inputs are programming errors, not recoverable conditions):
```
RuntimeException
  └── CacheException          — base for all cache errors; catch this to handle any
        ├── NullKeyException  — get(null) or put(null, v)
        └── NullValueException — put(k, null)
```

**`LRUCache` guards** — `get` rejects null keys; `put` rejects null keys and null values. `LinkedHashMap` does not support null keys when using `accessOrder=true`, so this also prevents a silent `NullPointerException` that would have leaked from inside the map.

**`Cache` interface** — unchanged signature-wise (unchecked exceptions don't appear in `throws` clauses), but any implementation is expected to enforce the same contract.
